parole.testo: Uncertain. Older attempts try to connect it to Latin dīrēctus (“direct; straight”), via borrowing from Catalan adret, a dretes or Old Occitan adreit, but phonological problems and in the case of Catalan, the word not being poorly attested, disprove this hypothesis. More likely, it is from Gothic 𐌰𐍄

parole.significato: to bring down, vanquish, conquer, topple, defeat
parole.testo: From Latin duplicāre, probably through the intermediate of Catalan doblegar in the 15th century, as it was not found earlier in Old Spanish texts and is completely absent in Portuguese as well. Doublet of duplicar, which was later borrowed directly from Latin.

Related to fuego, and possibly ultimately from a Vulgar Latin *focone, from focus, perhaps through Catalan fogó or through a Mozarabic intermediary, as it was attested relatively late and preserved the initial -f- as opposed to -h- (compare hogar, hoguera, hogaza, etc.). Cognate with Sicilian fucuni

Inherited from Old Spanish portar, a foreign word borrowed in various times from Latin portāre (“bring, carry”) and from cognates in Romance languages such as Catalan portar, French porter, Italian portare; ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *per- (“go, traverse”).

parole.significato: turron (a sweet made from almonds, similar to nougat)
parole.testo: Probably from Latin torrēre, possibly via Catalan torró. Cognate with Italian torrone, Sicilian turruni.
